notes: DNA v2 strings for instruments (DNA.md 5); kit maps are DNA v3 kit DNAs (PRESET-ENGINE-2.md 15.2): one k token per pad, kit strips built from Insert File segments (j = 1 the source, 2.. each insert).

Every NAME is a library sound on the disc: em_* recordings, ems_* synthesized, emh_* hybrids (catalog/electromech.json). Instruments set K to the first layer's root; other pitched layers get T = K - their root; unpitched layers are F (fixed).

Pitched sounds whose root is above C6 (or below C1) are folded by octaves into the playable range: the key plays the right pitch class, in the sound's own octave. Pitched kit pads get their root folded to the octave nearest the pad's key range.

Validated with design/v3/dna3.cpp (parse3, canonical3) against main's core/dna.cpp (-DCORE_KEEPS=1), with the full library name list: every source and insert resolves, every pad's layer and segment exist, length <= 1024.
The 3.11 edition has no library sounds of its own beyond its library drive; these presets need the library disc (both editions read it, DNA.md 5.5).

instruments.name: Relay Mallet
instruments.description: A relay armature striking a tuned steel bar; the modelled pull-in click rides on every note.

instruments.name: Relay Marimba
instruments.description: Undercut-bar ratios struck by a relay; the release tick follows as a second, softer click.

instruments.name: Relay Ping
instruments.description: Hybrid: a recorded relay click plus a tuned resonator ping.

instruments.name: Strowger Glock
instruments.description: Octave-doubled steel bar with a stepping-switch 'chunk' as the mallet.

instruments.name: Crossbar Gong
instruments.description: Hybrid: a crossbar operation with a struck gong body tuned to the key.

instruments.name: Teletype Bell Keyboard
instruments.description: The BEL bell as a keyboard; each note is preceded by the selector magnet's code clicks.

instruments.name: Exchange Ringer
instruments.description: Subscriber-set gong partials, octave-doubled, with the ringer relay's pull.

instruments.name: Register Drawer Bell
instruments.description: FM drawer bell with a recorded drawer/mechanism hit.

instruments.name: Typewriter Bell Keys
instruments.description: A recorded typewriter margin bell, key-tracked.

instruments.name: Margin Bell Lo-Fi
instruments.description: Bitcrushed teletype bell over a typebar strike.

instruments.name: GPO Alarm Bell
instruments.description: The exchange alarm bell from the 1933 GPO film, playable as a sustained pitched bell.

instruments.name: Signal Bell
instruments.description: A recorded signal bell with a clutch-trip click.

instruments.name: Phone Ring Keys
instruments.description: Western Electric 500 ringer as a pitched trill.

instruments.name: Line Printer Lead
instruments.description: Hammer volleys repeating at the note's rate (1403 'music'); a single hammer adds the attack.

instruments.name: 1403 Chorus
instruments.description: Octave-stacked, detuned printer-hammer buzz.

instruments.name: Ferranti Hoot
instruments.description: Square pulses quantized to a 240 us beat, the Mark 1's out-of-tune hoot.

instruments.name: CSIRAC Pulse
instruments.description: One-sample speaker pulses from a timing loop, crushed to 4 bits.

instruments.name: Modem Lead
instruments.description: FM built from the Bell 103 mark/space pair, through a telephone band.

instruments.name: RTTY Carrier Lead
instruments.description: The steady RTTY mark carrier as a pure, drifting lead.

instruments.name: Morse Buzzer Lead
instruments.description: A recorded Morse practice buzzer, key-tracked.

instruments.name: Modem Beep Lead
instruments.description: A recorded modem beep.

instruments.name: 1961 Vowel
instruments.description: Buzz source through 'ah' formants, a nod to the IBM 7094's 'Daisy Bell'.

instruments.name: Contact Spring
instruments.description: Karplus-Strong relay contact spring with a release tick.

instruments.name: Governor Spring Bass
instruments.description: A long, dark Karplus-Strong spring; a slice of the dial's wind-up for the attack.

instruments.name: Typewriter Pluck
instruments.description: Hybrid: a recorded typewriter key with a plucked spring tail.

instruments.name: Sounder Keys
instruments.description: A hollow FM tone with the sounder's click/clack on every key.

instruments.name: Tabulator Arp
instruments.description: One key plays a three-step arpeggio (root, fifth, octave) at the 407's 150-per-minute cycle (133 ms steps), over the tabulator's own cycle. The transposes of layers 2 and 3 are set below.

instruments.name: Drum Memory Drone
instruments.description: Drum whine, bearing hiss and head-select relays (IBM 650 drum at 12,500 rpm).

instruments.name: Motor Room
instruments.description: Additive motor drone tuned to the key, over a teletype motor bed.

instruments.name: Gear Whine Pad
instruments.description: Gear and capstan whine with speed hunting, four-voice unison.

instruments.name: Hum Bass
instruments.description: 60 Hz line hum and its odd harmonics as a bass; crackle underneath.

instruments.name: Transformer Bass
instruments.description: 50 Hz magnetostriction buzz as a growling bass.

instruments.name: Tube Hum Pad
instruments.description: A recorded tube-radio hum, key-tracked.

instruments.name: Electric Bell Drone
instruments.description: A recorded trembler bell as a pitched, buzzing drone.

instruments.name: Dial Tone Organ
instruments.description: 350 + 440 Hz dial tone as an organ, with a ring-modulated copy.

instruments.name: Switchroom Pad
instruments.description: Hybrid switchboard relays over a 50 Hz drone, with a pitched motor pad.

instruments.name: Newsroom
instruments.description: Two teletypes printing, one synthetic and one recorded, panned apart.

instruments.name: Relay Rain
instruments.description: A rack of relays operating, wide. Mod wheel (macro 1) swings the pan.

instruments.name: Digital Trunk
instruments.description: Hybrid: a recorded dial-up handshake bitcrushed to 4 bits, over crushed line noise.

instruments.name: Party Line
instruments.description: Crosstalk murmur, crackle and hum: a noisy party line. The hum layer follows the key.

kits.name: Relay Room
kits.description: Zuse/Bell Labs relay racks: pull and release pairs as velocity layers, chatter loops in a cut group, a pitched relay mallet on the upper keys.

kits.name: Card Room
kits.description: Hollerith to IBM 407: keypunch, card feed and stacker, tabulator cycle, sorter run, Hollerith bell. Loops are gated in one cut group.

kits.name: Teletype 33
kits.description: A Model 33 ASR as a kit: characters, CR, LF, bell, motor start and stop (one cut group), print bursts and the tape punch.

kits.name: Message Center
kits.description: Arrive, store, display: each row of keys is one event phrase broken into its parts. C2 row arrive (bell, motor, print, CR, LF), C3 row store (punch, card, drum, tape), C4 row display (line printer, split-flap, flip-disc, Selectric), C5 whole phrases.

kits.name: Line
kits.description: The telephone line: call-progress tones (one cut group, so a new tone replaces the last), pulse dialling, ringers, modem and RTTY tones, and the noises (hum, hiss, crackle, dropouts, crosstalk, hits).

kits.name: Strowger Exchange
kits.description: A step-by-step office: selector steps, vertical pulses, rotary hunt, release, crossbar and the recorded 500-point selector and switchboard; ringer gong pitched on the top keys.

kits.name: Telegraph Office
kits.description: Sounder click/clack, keyed phrases, CW tones, Morse buzzer, ticker, the news keyer and the radio-teletype modes.

kits.name: Calculator Bureau
kits.description: Comptometers, Fridens and registers: crank pulls, ratchets, division runs, cash register and its bell (pitched), time clock.

kits.name: Typing Pool
kits.description: Typebars, Selectric, electric and daisy-wheel machines, margin bells, carriage returns.

kits.name: Mainframe Hall
kits.description: 1950s-60s machine room: line printer, vacuum-column tape, drum memory, card reader, and the first computer-music voices (Ferranti hoot, CSIRAC pulse) pitched on the top keys.

kits.name: Signal Bells
kits.description: Bells of the machine age: BEL, margin bells, trembler and alarm bells, the GPO exchange alarm, ringers, the desk-calculator bell. Most pads fixed; three pitched in a narrow range.

kits.name: Solenoid Lab
kits.description: Actuator physics: the modelled plunger in its variants (pull, release, bounce, tiny, large) beside recorded solenoids, contactors and relays. Pull pads mute the held buzz; release pads answer note-off where gated.
